findings.issue_text: getSubGroupsCount() returns null when its delegate is concurrently deleted, violating GroupModel’s never-null contract and exposing null subgroup counts to callers
The reader thread is not synchronized to make at least one request before deletion begins, so the test can pass without exercising concurrent access
The test asserts immediately after setting the stop flag without joining the reader thread, allowing an in-flight failure after the assertion and leaving a worker thread running

goldens.comment: Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() violates the GroupModel contract (Javadoc says it never returns null) and may lead to NPEs in callers that expect a non-null count.
The reader thread isn’t waited for; flipping deletedAll to true and asserting immediately can race and miss exceptions added just after the flag change, making this test flaky.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The reader thread is not synchronized to make at least one request before deletion begins, so the test can pass without exercising concurrent access

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a race condition in the test design. Looking at the diff, the test starts a reader thread and immediately proceeds to delete groups. There's no synchronization mechanism (like a CountDownLatch or barrier) to ensure the reader thread has made at least one request before deletions begin. The reader thread could start, check `deletedAll.get()` which is already true (if deletions complete very fast), and exit without ever making a request. This is a legitimate test design flaw that could cause the test to pass without actually exercising the concurrent access scenario it's meant to test.
